subject: POC performance gating: MAP, throughput results, and econ checkpoint
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@finpulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC performance MAP & throughput gating

Sarah —

Following our call today, attached is a compact MAP for the POC focused on throughput gating and unit economics. The goal: validate that the POC meets the sustained-throughput and TTFT targets that you listed, and to produce a small handoff package for a canary launch.

High level asks from FinPulse: sustained QPS >= 200 req/s (50–80 avg tokens/output), TTFT < 150 ms p50 and p95 < 300 ms, and tail latency behavior under concurrency patterns.

What we propose in the MAP (attached FinPulse_MAP_v2.xlsx):
- Phase A (Week 0–1): controlled benchmarking (our infra) — throughput sweeps, concurrency ramps, and a stability window (10 min sustained) at target QPS.
- Phase B (Week 2): on-customer canary: same workload replay against dedicated pool + routing policy, 24–48h monitoring.
- Gate criteria: sustained QPS achieved for 10 continuous minutes, token/sec numbers within 10% of baseline, TTFT and p95 within targets, and unit-econ within agreed band.

We've scheduled a Redwood perf run on our staging cluster tomorrow morning; I will send the results immediately after the run (we'll include raw CSV and a 1-page econ snapshot). Can you confirm the target avg output tokens we should use for request modelling? You mentioned 60 tokens on the call — want to lock that in.

Also, please confirm the decision date for the canary (we suggest Oct 15 to align with your release window).

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: FinPulse_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP workbook, milestones + gating criteria)

From: Sarah Park <sarah@finpulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ryan Chen <ryan@finpulse.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC performance MAP & throughput gating

Karthik —

Thanks for the MAP. Confirming: use avg output 60 tokens for modeling. The key gating points from our side: sustained 200 req/s for 10 minutes, TTFT p50 < 120ms (we can tolerate up to 150ms briefly), and p95 < 280ms. Also want a short unit-econ table that converts to $/1M tokens and $/req so our finance folks can sign off quickly.

Decision timeline: our PMs need an internal review by Oct 12; if the MAP passes, we'll approve the canary for Oct 15.

Ryan will coordinate infra access for the canary phase.

-Sarah
VP Product, FinPulse

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@finpulse.com>, Ryan Chen <ryan@finpulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC performance MAP & throughput gating — initial perf run results

Team —

We completed the first controlled throughput sweep this morning (attached throughput_results_oct01.csv and a short unit econ PDF). Key takeaways (staging cluster, mixed sequence lengths that mirror your production prompt distribution, avg output 60 tokens):

- Sustained QPS: 212 req/s sustained for 10 minutes at concurrency = 28 (steady-state).
- Tokens/sec: 12,720 tokens/sec at the 212 req/s point (avg 60 tokens per request).
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): p50 = 92 ms, p95 = 205 ms.
- End-to-end latency (completion): p50 = 340 ms, p95 = 780 ms (these include generation time for 60 tokens).
- Concurrency behavior: stable response tail up to concurrency 48; beyond that we see queuing and p95 increases ~20% per 10 additional concurrent streams.

Unit economics (staging costs, normalized):
- Raw inference compute cost: ~$2.50 per 1M tokens (model runtime on our GPU fleet).
- Effective per-request cost (avg 60 tokens): ~$0.15 per 1k requests -> rephrased: $0.0025 per 1k tokens.
- Estimated GPU-hours to produce 1M tokens: ~0.06 GPU-hours (varies by model/quantization).
- Suggested customer-facing pricing band for POC (for comparison): $2.75–$3.25 per 1M tokens (covers infra variance + monitoring overhead).

Attachments include raw CSV of the sweep and the 1-page econ snapshot. Caveats: these numbers are from our staging pool (shared infra). For the canary on dedicated capacity we expect p95 latencies to tighten by ~10–15% and unit-econ to shift slightly depending on committed capacity and burst profile.

Next steps proposed:
- Confirm metrics ok to present to FinPulse PM (Sarah) and Finance (Oct 12 internal review).
- If green, schedule canary Oct 15 on a dedicated pool sized for sustained 220 req/s (we recommend two reserved instances + autoscale buffer).
- Marissa & Neha from our side will publish the canary runbook and monitoring dashboard.

Karthik

Attachments: throughput_results_oct01.csv, unit_econ_snapshot.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC performance MAP & throughput gating — pricing/discount note

Quick note for the thread before we share externally: finance asked whether we can offer a POC pricing cap for the canary phase to limit FinPulse exposure. Suggested approach:
- Offer a capped monthly commit for the month of Oct equivalent to $3.00 per 1M tokens with a usage true-up at month end.
- Include a performance SLA clause in the MAP: if sustained QPS < 85% of target during canary for >2 consecutive windows, we will provide a credit equal to 10% of the month's POC charges.

Neha, can you prepare the short SOW language and update FinPulse_MAP_v2.xlsx with the commit/credit rows? Ben, please prepare a concise monitoring dashboard link for the PM review (metrics: rolling 10m QPS, p95 TTFT, tokens/sec).

-Marissa

From: Sarah Park <sarah@finpulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Ryan Chen <ryan@finpulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC performance MAP & throughput gating — approval for canary

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the run results. This looks promising and within the tolerance band. Finance is comfortable with the capped POC pricing and the SLA credit language Marissa proposed.

Decision: FinPulse approves the canary for Oct 15 if the dedicated pool is provisioned and the updated MAP (with commit/credit language) is sent by Oct 9. Ryan will coordinate infra credentials and monitoring access.

Please treat Oct 9 as the cutoff for any material changes to gating criteria.

-Sarah
